$comment: Single source of truth for the immutable refs that ci.yml and release.yml pin each sibling backend checkout to (§17 pin B). Each pinned commit CONTAINS the committed contract artifacts the gen:* drivers regenerate from: docs/schema.json, docs/flows.json, docs/errors.json, docs/capabilities.json (+ pyproject.toml for the manifest backend-version pin). Bumping a pin is a deliberate PR after the backend releases a new contract — never float main. Procedure: CONTRIBUTING.md, section 'Contract pins'. 2026-07-16: bumped to the v1-canon-sweep release tags (§60, api-versioning.md) — auth v0.5.8, notifications v0.3.8, profiles v0.3.13, billing v0.4.11, workspaces v0.4.2, calendar v0.3.4, recordings v0.3.2; all contracts now carry /<mod>/api/v1/ paths; react gen:* artifacts regenerated against these refs in the same change. 2026-08-09: the Spanish wave — auth v0.20.1, notifications v0.7.1, billing v0.6.1, workspaces v0.22.1 bumped to the releases that carry translations/errors.es.json (profiles was already there; calendar and recordings ship no locale catalogues at all and are deliberately left behind, so their pairs stay en-only rather than gaining a fabricated empty one). Each note below states what the bump drags in BESIDES the catalogue. 2026-08-23: stapel-video v0.7.0 joins the pins — the first entry added FOR a pair rather than under one: nothing in this repo read stapel-video before, and the release that gave ParticipantSpan a scope_key is the only reason @stapel/video-react exists. It is also the first pin whose gen:errors runs with ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core (the module ships no translations/ of its own). 2026-08-23: stapel-billing v0.6.1 -> v0.8.1 — the wallet body grows lots[], holds[] and expiring_soon, which is the whole reason @stapel/billing-react's useWallet and its new /default <WalletPanel/> exist; the same span prunes the core-owned error keys out of billing's own translations/, so the ru/es bundles now depend on the stapel-core merge that was already in place.

stapel-geo.note: release v0.4.1 - 2026-08-30: adds GET /geo/api/v1/ip, the centre a map opens on before the browser's position prompt is answered - or after it is refused, which is a supported answer and not an error. The verb ALWAYS answers something a map can open on: an unknown range, a private address, a missing database or a provider that raised all come back 200 with the deployment fallback centre and ip_resolved:false, and only a deployment with no locator answer AND no fallback centre answers 204. That shape is why geo-react useResolvedLocation can be a three-rung ladder (browser fix -> IP city -> configured centre) with one branch instead of an error path. map/config.endpoints gained "ip", so the pair still learns every path from the server. Behind it: the IP_LOCATORS merge-registry (offline MaxMind via the stapel-geo[ipgeo] extra, or a single configured static point), and IP_TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH / IP_CLIENT_IP_RESOLVER, which count X-Forwarded-For from the RIGHT so a caller-forged prefix cannot pick its own city. Checks W008/W009/W010. 2026-08-26: geo-react ships ru+es locale bundles. release 0.4.0 - the release that made a location a HUMAN thing and the only reason @stapel/geo-react can exist. Until 0.4.0 the module shipped coordinates and called it a feature, which is how a live listing composer ended up with two raw fields named latitude and longitude; 0.4.0 adds GET map/config (public - the tile layer, its ATTRIBUTION OBLIGATION, the search discipline, and the endpoint table a client is asked to read its four other paths from) and GET geocoding/resolve (one round trip: display line, address components, alternatives, geohash, opt-in nearest Location rows), which are the two calls the default picker is built on. What is read here: docs/schema.json (12 paths under /geo/api/v1/, 12 component schemas - MapConfig, TileLayer, GeocodeResponse/Feature/Geometry/Properties and PlaceResolution/PlaceSummary are the ones this pair generates against), docs/errors.json (50 codes: 8 owned by stapel_geo, 42 cross-cutting stapel_core) and pyproject.toml 0.4.0 -> backend.contract >=0.4 <0.5. docs/flows.json carries two flows (geo.pick_location, geo.geocode_address); the pair drives the pick from a bag rather than a flow machine, because the steps are a finger on a map and a browser permission prompt, neither of which the server sequences. LOCALES: no translations/ directory, so gen:errors runs with ERRORS_LOCALES=ru, ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core's catalogue and ERRORS_LOCALE_EXEMPT_OWNERS=stapel_geo - the 42 cross-cutting keys come from core in ru, the 8 geo keys are authored by the pair in its own ./i18n/ru until upstream localizes them. THE REFUSALS THIS PAIR IS SHAPED BY: 401/403 on the four geocoding verbs is the DEFAULT permission (GEOCODER_PERMISSIONS), so 'geocoding is not available to me' is a first-class state and NOT an error - the map renders and the pin drops for an anonymous visitor, only the address is missing; 429 is the server asking for quiet and keeps the last good suggestions on screen rather than replacing them with a red box; error.502.geocoder_unavailable is the one retryable failure, where every 400 is not; and a SUCCESSFUL call with zero features is an empty state (the middle of a lake has coordinates too), which is why nothing in the pair folds an empty answer into a failure.

stapel-attributes.note: release v0.6.0 - 2026-08-31: the composite `group` kind - one feature holding a small TABLE (config {type:'group', fields:[FeatureDef...], repeat:{min,max}|null}, DTO value a list of rows keyed by child slug, DAO rows whose cells are the children's own DAOs with their DaoMeta). Nesting depth is 1, a child may not be a header, and a child may not carry `rules` - all three enforced by validate_config, because the rule engine reads a flat map of top-level slugs and a rule inside a row could never fire, so a rule written on a child would be accepted and never match. docs/feature-def.schema.json gains $defs.GroupConfig / $defs.GroupRepeat, which is what src/generated/featureDef.ts emits GroupConfig from (gen:feature-def), and tests/golden/declarations.json now lists thirteen builtin types - the list test/fixtures/attributes-registry.json pins. release v0.5.1 - 2026-08-30: attributes v2. 0.5.0 is the rule engine (rules.py: evaluate_rules/narrow_config/parse_rules over the closed grammar), FeatureDef v2 (rules, description, example, default, hints, group), the ref-vocabulary protocol (vocabularies.py, register_vocabulary_resolver) and the two ref types (ref_select, ref_hierarchical_select); docs/feature-def.schema.json is the §68 canon @stapel/attributes-react generates src/generated/featureDef.ts from (gen:feature-def), and tests/golden/rules/ is the SHARED corpus gen:rules copies into the pair (59 cases + 10 pipeline). 0.5.1 adds tests/golden/rules/avito/{prose,values-by-group}.json - 3890 distinct rules recorded from the Avito import, both polarities per rule, expectations written by the Python evaluator - which the pair runs through its own evaluateRules so a split-brain between the two implementations is a red test rather than a production divergence. stapel-vocabularies.note: release v0.1.0 - 2026-08-30: the NEW L2 module @stapel/vocabularies-react is the pair of, and the reason it exists. A ref feature carries a POINTER to a vocabulary level rather than an options list, because the lists do not fit in a category schema (529 phone vendors, 14962 models), so the terms arrive over a second wire this module serves. What is read here: docs/schema.json (4 paths under /vocabularies/api/v1/, 4 component schemas - Vocabulary, Level, Term, TermPage; the two the pair is built on are GET vocabularies/{slug}/terms/ (level, parent, q, limit, offset -> {results, total}) and GET vocabularies/{slug}/terms/resolve/ (level, codes -> {code: label}, unknown codes omitted)), docs/errors.json, docs/flows.json (literally [] - the module annotates no @flow_step, the stapel-categories precedent) and pyproject.toml 0.1.0 -> backend.contract >=0.1 <0.2. LOCALES: no translations/ directory, so gen:errors runs with ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core's catalogue and ERRORS_LOCALE_EXEMPT_OWNERS=stapel_vocabularies - the cross-cutting keys come from core in ru/es, the module's own three (vocabulary_not_found, level_not_found, bad_parent) are authored by the pair in its own ./i18n/<locale> until upstream localizes them. THE SEAM: attributes-react declares the VocabularyClient interface (two functions) and this pair SATISFIES it structurally - neither package imports the other, and the container hands createVocabularyClient's result to VocabularyClientProvider.
